Net MRR movement follows the timeframe buttons · stripe style
Numbers and chart both follow the timeframe buttons: daily up to 30d, calendar weeks starting Monday up to 180d, calendar months for 1y, last bucket is the current partial. Green is MRR gained from joins, rejoins and upgrades, red is MRR lost to cancels and downgrades, gold is the net. Upgrades are tracked two ways: the daily refresh diff catches them live, and Pull all-time data backfills the full history from invoice prices — every past upgrade lands on the day it billed.
Reconciliation check vs stripe dashboard
Refresh to populate.
Compare these against the Stripe dashboard after each refresh. Failed checkouts are created-then-never-paid subscriptions, excluded from members, new subs, cancels and churn. MRR here is list price minus ongoing coupons, EUR at the live ECB rate, so expect within a couple of % of Stripe, not penny-identical. Stripe stays source of truth.

Refresh data to build reports.
How this works: a forecast locks on the 1st from your last six months and never changes, so the month is judged like guidance. Nothing is graded until 15% of the month has run. The full explainer is under How this works above.
How this works: on the 1st of each month the terminal locks a forecast for the month from your last six months of data: how many people join, how many paying members cancel, what Elite upgrades add, and what all of that does to MRR. Once locked it never changes, so the month is judged against the number that was on the table at the start, like guidance. The likely range is how far the forecast has been wrong before, measured on your own history, not theory. The target is the ambitious end of that range, set higher on purpose: something to aim at, not a prediction. Beating, on pace and behind compare what has happened so far with where the forecast says you should be by today, along a straight line from the 1st to month end. Nothing is graded until 15% of the month has run. Past months use only the data that existed before each month began. Cash rows appear once Pull all-time data has run.

Quick ratio

£ gained ÷ £ lost each month. The dots swing on small numbers — the smooth line (3-month average) is the signal.

Net revenue retention %

Of members you already had at the start of each month, how much of their £ was still paying at the end. Judge your own trend, not SaaS folklore benchmarks.
Revenue by tier monthly · is Elite growing its share?
If the gold band grows faster than the blue, upsells are working — Elite pays 2.1× Pro.
MRR over time reconstructed from subscription history
Built from paid-start and Stripe-metric end dates at each subscription's current Stripe price. Scheduled cancellations end MRR when requested; access can continue separately until period end. Historical price changes and expired coupons are not backfilled by Stripe, so older £ values remain approximate.
Locked forecast vs current expected the plan froze at period start · the expected line moves with the data
The locked column is set once — at the start of the month (or quarter) — and never changes, so it's an honest bar to judge the period against. Current expected re-projects from today's data every refresh. Gap green = tracking ahead of the plan you set; red = behind it.

Does credit actually save people? SAVE credit only — a referrer's £20 says nothing about whether a save worked
Credit per month save credit and referral credit are different spends — never blended
Voided = a failed invoice written off. Free month = a skipped billing period or a £0-paid renewal. Discounted = a renewal paid under the tier price (the £18-on-£28 save). Referral = the £20 refer-a-friend reward paid to the REFERRER when someone redeems their code — acquisition spend, matched one-per-redemption and never counted as a save. First invoices never count (the entry offer is a product, not credit), and £5/£20 AI-credit payments are excluded. Tag which codes are referrals on the Attribution page.

MRR forecast median-anchored model · band from measured error
How the forecast works: each month is built from your last six months: joins, returning members, Elite upgrades, cancels and downgrades, each anchored on the median so one unusual month cannot become the trend. Expansion is capped by the pool of mature Pros who have not yet been offered Elite, cancels never go below the best month on record, and the band is the size of the model's own past errors. The gold line is the forecast, the green dashes are the target trajectory from the Goals page. Seasonal multipliers are measured from your own months and shown below the chart.

Churn rate by acquisition channel chart = steady 90-day monthly rate · 30d snapshot in the table · channels under 30 members muted
Not enough attributed members yet to compare channels. Run Pull all-time data in Settings to sweep older sessions.
Same maths as Stripe's subscriber churn rate chart, split by channel: subscribers whose Stripe-metric MRR reached zero in the last 30 days ÷ (subscribers 30 days ago + first-time subscribers activated inside the window). Trial bails never count — someone only becomes a subscriber once money starts — but a new joiner who churns in the same window counts on both sides. Stripe counts a scheduled cancellation from the request time and a paused collection from the first observed pause; both remain visible separately while there is still time to save or resume them. Untracked is everyone who joined before the checkout dropdown existed — those sources can't be recovered, so this bucket only fades as older members age out and tracked joiners take over. Members with an affiliate code always count in the Affiliate row even if they also picked a dropdown source. Small channels are muted: too few members to read a rate from. The All members row tracks the Subscriber churn rate figure on your Stripe dashboard. Churn % · 30d is that same trailing-30-day window — it moves day to day as cancels enter and leave the window, especially on small channels. Avg monthly · 90d window is the same maths over the last 90 days, shown per month — three times the data, so it barely moves day to day. Judge channels on that column; the LTV figures run off it too.

Appearance this browser

Vault is the Resell Vault navy. Glass and Frost are the liquid-glass looks, dark and light, with frosted panes over a slow aurora. Graphite is a neutral dark. Paper is the plain light theme. Charts follow the theme.

This browser only

Opens in its own window, with an icon in your dock or home screen. Same login, same data.
Backup files contain member names and emails but never keys — store them privately.

Data imports

Discord join and leave data comes only from the Invite Tracker analytics export. Everything else the terminal needs arrives from Stripe through the cloud runner.
Upload the analytics CSV from Invite Tracker (any window; 90 days is ideal). Exact event data replaces older estimates for the same days, new days are added, and re-uploading the same file changes nothing.
